item.title: A Spacious Coastal Home Overlooking The Minch
item.description: West coast light, sea views to Skye and Harris, and a home with separate apartment and letting pod near Gairloch combine to create a rare Highland property with both calm living and income potential worth exploring.The post A Spacious Coastal Home Overlooking The Minch appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Highland Jobs is Becoming Part of Everyday Life Across The Highlands
item.description: Highland Jobs is steadily becoming part of everyday hiring across the Highlands, offering a simple £39 flat fee model that is building trust among employers and applicants and strengthening local digital infrastructure.The post Highland Jobs is Becoming Part of Everyday Life Across The Highlands appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: £130,000 Refurbishment Programme Begins Across Moray Libraries
item.description: A £130,000 refurbishment programme is beginning across Moray libraries, with temporary closures in Forres and Elgin as brighter, modernised spaces are created to support learning, creativity and community use.The post £130,000 Refurbishment Programme Begins Across Moray Libraries appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: A9 Tomatin Junction To Close as Temporary Access Opens From 20 February
item.description: The Tomatin junction on the A9 will close from 20 February 2026 as a new temporary junction opens 400 metres south, with overnight traffic signals on 19 February and permanent bus stop relocations in place. The post A9 Tomatin Junction To Close as Temporary Access Opens From 20 February appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Seventeen Farming Sites Opened To New Entrants Across Scotland
item.description: Forestry and Land Scotland has opened applications for 17 farming sites totalling 325 hectares, offering grazing opportunities for new entrants and young farmers across Scotland.The post Seventeen Farming Sites Opened To New Entrants Across Scotland appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: UHI Inverness Graduates Step Straight Into Civil Engineering Interviews
item.description: Eleven UHI Inverness students graduated from the CECA Scotland Academy before heading straight into job interviews with leading civil engineering firms, highlighting strong demand in Scotland’s £4.5 billion infrastructure sector.The post UHI Inverness Graduates Step Straight Into Civil Engineering Interviews appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Why I am Standing With Alba and What That Means for The Highlands and Islands
item.description: Laura Hänsler has announced she is standing with Alba, citing her A9 road safety campaign and calling for energy fairness so Highland communities see real benefit from the infrastructure they host.The post Why I am Standing With Alba and What That Means for The Highlands and Islands appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Highland Council Bus Service Delivers Savings and Passenger Growth
item.description: Highland Council’s in house bus service has expanded to 25 vehicles, avoided significant contract costs and carried more than 135,000 passengers in 2025 as plans for a long term operating model move forward.The post Highland Council Bus Service Delivers Savings and Passenger Growth appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Spey Viaduct Consent Application Submitted as Clearance Works Begin
item.description: Moray Council has submitted Listed Building Consent to remove two failed sections of the Spey Viaduct after its partial collapse, while vegetation clearance begins along Stynie Road to support diversion routes.The post Spey Viaduct Consent Application Submitted as Clearance Works Begin appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Local MP and MSP Respond as Orbex Enters Administration
item.description: MP And MSP Respond As Orbex Enters Administration Forres based space launch company Orbex is entering administration, prompting calls for urgent government action from local representatives. Moray West, Nairn and Strathspey MP Graham Leadbitter said the decision places around 160 jobs at risk and criticised the UK Government’s handling of funding.
